title: Aurionpro Solutions Ltd - 532668 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: FY26 revenue grew 20.2% to INR 1,411 crore, but Q4 missed plan on Middle East deal slippage and hyperscaler revenue timing; no FY27 growth number given.
summary.overview: Management said FY26 was below its own standards: revenue rose 20.2% to INR 1,411 crore, with EBITDA margin at 20.02% and PAT margin at 15.02%, toward the lower end of guided ranges. The original plan was close to 30% growth, and Q4 fell short on Middle East license deal closures and project completions, a delayed hyperscaler data center project, and a one-time labour code charge. Management is stepping up expensed and capitalised investment in AI-native banking software, transit back-office software, payments and data centers, and expects higher working capital and balance-sheet pressure in FY27. It declined to give a numerical FY27 growth guide, saying only that it expects to grow ahead of industry rates.

segments.name: Banking
segments.commentary: Banking is slightly above 50% of revenue, per management's mix view. Q4 license revenue from Transaction Banking and interact deals slipped, mainly in Middle East. The company launched a fully AI-native trade finance platform on agentic architecture.

segments.name: Transit (TIG)
segments.commentary: Transit is slightly below half of revenue, with large strategic wins in India and a stronger global push. Management said TIG could grow slightly faster in FY27 because of larger orders, but the long-run mix is roughly a wash.

segments.name: Data center
segments.commentary: Won one of India's largest AI data center mandates from a hyperscaler, a INR 350 crore deal, and several other wins. Execution started ahead of revenue, and a large chunk of revenue is expected within FY27. Management described it as pure services, capital-light, with design, integrated engineering and program management.

segments.name: Europe (Fenixys)
segments.commentary: Management said Fenixys is growing strongly, has added clients, and is expanding into the Middle East, South Africa and the US. Recent European wins are smaller than Middle East deals, and management expects FY27 to be a good year for Europe.

segments.name: Payments
segments.commentary: Management said payments is becoming a meaningful revenue driver with a large merchant base, and that it will become more sizable in FY27. No revenue figure was given.

segments.name: NBFC platform
segments.commentary: Management said it has more than 30 NBFC clients and is competitive in the segment. Deal values are small, so not all wins are announced.

guidance_outlook: No numerical FY27 revenue growth guidance. Management said it will grow ahead of industry rates and that FY27 growth could match prior-year rates, to be reassessed in a quarter or two.
Management expects margins not to dip significantly from FY26 levels as order size grows. Analysts raised the possibility of a fall toward 15%-16%, which management did not endorse.
Management expects a short spurt of capitalised and expensed investment, tapering over the next couple of quarters, with a larger upfront investment year than usual in FY27.
Management expects no debt increase in FY27. Pressure is expected in working capital and growth-oriented balance-sheet items.
Management expects Middle East deal activity to restart, though not at full pace. It expects the MEA slowdown may extend into Q1 FY27.
capex_capacity: Capex is rising sharply in H2 FY26. Intangibles plus intangibles under development are close to INR 200 crore, up from about INR 20 crore and INR 30 crore in earlier years, per the analyst.

Investment areas: AI-native software stacks across trade finance, transaction banking, lending and new product lines; tabular foundation model research (Orion MSP, next version expected in about 8 weeks); transit back-office software for MMRDA and CCHS; payments; and cybersecurity.
Management said a large part of the development spend will be routed to the P&L where client projects back it. Some will be built ahead of client contracts and capitalised.
Transit software stack work for MMRDA is described as a one-off, with later spend expected to be expensed.
Data center: investment in long-lead project execution ahead of revenue recognition, with some of the early work deferred into Q1 FY27.
demand_pricing: Middle East: banks halted late-stage buying processes in Q4. Management said some restarts of deal activity and POCs are now visible, but full buying has not resumed. Pre-war Saudi bank wins are in execution but have been slowed by inability to station teams on site.

Banking demand: management said win rates are exceptional and that it sees no material change in software buying behaviour or contract tenor. Banks are weighing AI spending against other priorities, which may slow decisions.

Competition from frontier AI labs: management said it sees no immediate threat to core banking software from firms such as Anthropic, citing the trade finance agent launch as evidence of AI-native product superiority.

Pricing: management did not address pricing pressure directly. It said that larger contracts (INR 100-350 crore) are carrying higher working capital and that contracting and payment terms are being tightened.

Cross-sell: average banking relationships are about 2 products per bank (up from about 1.5), with some banks using 5 or 6 products. Management said mature software could grow 10%-12% without new logos.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 and FY28 margins and revenue growth return to 30%, or stay at current levels?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a number, citing Middle East and macro uncertainty. It said demand has not changed, Q4 was a management miss, and it expects to beat industry growth.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the capex increase is for TIG versus other areas, and where will intangibles stabilise?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex is for TIG (transit and data center), the banking stack, AI stack, payments and cybersecurity. Management described a short-term spurt over the next couple of quarters, with products rebuilt as AI-native versions.

qa_highlights.question: How much R&D was spent in FY26 and how much in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management's best guess is INR 150-200 crore over the next four quarters, subject to productivity gains from AI-based code generation. The company has spent heavily on AI development over the last six months.

qa_highlights.question: What is the hyperscaler deal and when will its revenue be recognised?
qa_highlights.answer: The INR 350 crore hyperscaler deal faced planning delays. Management said a fairly large chunk of revenue will be recognised within FY27, and the data center business is pure services.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital requirement in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said INR 200-250 crore is the right number, with efforts to tighten contracting and payment terms. It does not expect debt to rise.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR 1,800 crore order book executable, and how might Middle East stress affect inflows?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated 68%-72% of the order book is executable over 12 months, constrained by supply chain and Middle East issues. It said it is moving resources closer to Middle East customers and pushing Southeast Asia and Europe.

risks_watch: Middle East: prolonged geopolitical conflict could continue to delay license deal closures and project execution, and Q1 FY27 may also be affected.
Margin and working capital: front-ended investment, larger contracts and an INR 200-250 crore working capital need could compress margins and cash flow if revenue timing slips again.
Revenue visibility: only 68%-72% of the INR 1,800 crore order book is expected to be executable within 12 months, and the hyperscaler revenue timing has already slipped once.
AI disruption: management acknowledged that the pace of AI change may affect contract tenure, but it sees no immediate threat to core banking software from frontier model firms.

Watch in Q1 FY27: Middle East deal restarts, data center revenue conversion, the trade finance AI platform rollout across the stack, the next Orion MSP release, and whether intangible and development spend tapers.
summary.management_tone: Candid and self-critical on Q4 and FY26 execution, while confident about long-term demand. It is evasive on FY27 numerical guidance, citing uncertainty in the Middle East and macro conditions. On investment, it is emphatic that front-ended spend is necessary.
key_quotes: By our own standards, the final result was below par. We can do better and we will.
We would rather absorb temporary balance sheet pressure than underinvest when the opportunity is this clear to us.
I would think the number is somewhere between 150 and 200 crores over the next four quarters, but we are working very hard to drive productivity improvements and try to shrink it.
We enter FY27 with an order book exceeding 1800 crores and a healthy pipeline across all segments.

adds.what: Data center services mandate (INR 350 crore hyperscaler deal) - pure services, capital-light; not physical capacity

growth.why: No numerical FY27 revenue guide; management says it will grow ahead of industry and FY27 could match prior-year rates, backed by an order book above INR 1,800 crore (68-72% executable) and a large INR 350 crore data center mandate, though Middle East deal activity is stalled and the brief gives no quantified growth.
